Article Title: AIIMS Delhi displays live population count of India: How does it get data on newly born babies?
Article Text:
AIIMS population display (Instagram)

A population clock, not a birth register

So why the number keeps changing

India's last completed population Census

​A population clock (Instagram)

What about babies born at AIIMS?

Why does the clock look so precise?

A digital clock is going viral in Delhi. Well, it’s not an ordinary clock. It’s a population counter clock which is displayed at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS Delhi). It has recently attracted attention online, with the number on the screen changing continuously and appearing to show India’s population growing every second. Now, this viral display has also raised an important question: if the number increases every few seconds, is AIIMS actually receiving information every time a baby is born somewhere in India?So the answer is NO.It’s a population clock and it is an estimate based on demographic data and population projections. It’s not a nationwide live birth-tracking system. The distinction is important because India does have official systems for recording births and deaths. These systems do not work like a real-time national counter.The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s National Health Profile identifies the Census, registration of vital events, population surveys, population projections and the Sample Registration System (SRS) among the sources used for demographic information.The Civil Registration System (CRS), maintained through the registration machinery of the government, is responsible for the continuous recording of vital events such as births and deaths. The Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner describes civil registration as the continuous, permanent and compulsory recording of the occurrence and characteristics of vital events.But this does not mean that a national population display receives an electronic notification every time a birth takes place in India.Now this is where population estimation comes in. A population clock takes a known or estimated population at a particular reference point and applies demographic rates to project how that population changes over time.If the estimated population is expected to rise by a certain number over a year, the annual change can be mathematically distributed across months, days, hours, minutes and seconds. A digital display can therefore make the number appear to be changing in real time.If the display increases by one, it does not necessarily mean that a particular baby has just been born somewhere in India. It represents a calculated movement in the estimated population total.India's last completed population Census was conducted in 2011, when the country's population was recorded at about 121.1 crore. The National Health Profile notes that India's population was projected to increase from 121.1 crore in 2011 to 152.2 crore by 2036, an increase of about 25% over 25 years.The United Nations follows a similar demographic approach. Its World Population Prospects 2024 provides population estimates and projections based on analyses of historical demographic trends for countries and territories around the world.The fact that the clock is located at AIIMS can easily create another misconception that AIIMS might somehow be using its maternity records to calculate India's population.Instead, births are recorded through the country's civil registration framework, while demographic agencies use registration data, surveys and statistical methods to understand population trends.That is perhaps the most fascinating part of the viral display.A computer can calculate an estimated population to several decimal places and refresh the display every second. That does not mean demographers know the exact number of people alive in India at that precise second.The changing digits are essentially a visualisation of a statistical model. It is similar to a countdown or a continuously updated financial index: the display can change every second even though the underlying information is based on data collected over a longer period.The viral AIIMS population clock is therefore best understood as a demographic awareness tool, not as a nationwide surveillance mechanism for births.India's population is certainly changing continuously. Babies are being born, people are dying and migration changes the distribution of people across regions. So, the next time the AIIMS population clock ticks upward, it does not mean that a computer has just received the birth certificate of another Indian baby.

It’s a population counter clock which is displayed at all india institute of medical sciences (aiims delhi) it has recently attracted attention online, with the number on the screen changing continuously. This has raised an important question: is aiims actually receiving information every time a baby is born somewhere in india?

Article Title: Will address colleagues’ genuine concern: Isro chief
Article Text:
Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) Chairman V Narayanan addresses a press conference

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Isro chairman V Narayanan Monday said genuine concerns of his colleagues would be clarified. “...If one or two people give you a letter, one cannot give a written communication immediately. Please understand, we are 20,000 employees. But we will address the employees,” he said on the sidelines of Bengaluru Space Expo 2026 here.Narayanan said that Isro had a system to regularly talk to employees. “...For example, when the space sector reforms were rolled out, from the Chairman onwards, we have regularly engaged with our employees,” he added.Earlier at the inaugural, Isro chairman and IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka made a strong case for greater participation by industry, startups and academia in India’s space programme, arguing that the country’s expanding ambitions cannot be met by the national space agency alone.Their remarks came a day after Isro and Goenka had released separate statements about the role of Isro, IN-SPACe and the private sector, which followed a letter by nine employees’ associations raising concerns over the future role of Isro.Narayanan said Monday that India’s requirements were set to rise sharply: “Our space programme is 64-65 years old. Right now, we have 56 space assets in serving the common man of the country.But the [future] need is huge. I think you all know that,” he said, adding that industry would need to play a greater role in meeting that.He said industry had, in any case, long been an integral part of India's space programme. “Whenever an LVM3 is lifting off or a GSLV is lifting off, please do not think that everything is done in Isro. Almost 80% of the budget is invested in Indian industry. About 450 industries are working for us now,” he said.Narayanan said the growth of private companies and startups had to be welcomed if India was to meet its future requirements. From only one or two space startups around the time of the 2020 reforms, the country now has more than 450, he said.But he stressed that greater private-sector participation did not mean a reduced role for Isro. The agency's role was evolving as it took on an expanding range of programmes, including Chandrayaan-4 and Chandrayaan-5, the Venus Orbiter Mission, the Indian Space Station, a next-generation launch vehicle and the expansion of the Navic constellation.India's current capability to launch around 8,500-9,000 kg would also have to be raised to about 30,000 kg, he said. “Isro's role is in no way reduced. But we also have to handhold startup companies and the private sector.”Goenka, meanwhile, said India was building a “full-spectrum space economy” in which Isro, IN-SPACe, Nsil, private industry, MSMEs, academia and investors would play reinforcing roles.From a single space startup in 2014, India now has more than 450, with over $160 million of private investment coming into the sector this year, he said. He urged established suppliers and MSMEs to move beyond supplying components and enter higher-value segments.“You are the quiet backbone of this story today,” Goenka told industry representatives, noting that a substantial share of what Isro builds already comes from its industrial suppliers. He urged them to move “from components to subsystems to full solutions” and serve global supply chains as well.
Article Summary: Isro chairman v narayanan said genuine concerns of his colleagues would be clarified. Narayanan said india’s requirements were set to rise sharply. From only one or two space startups around the time of the 2020 reforms, the country now has more than 450.

Article Title: 'Space ecosystem has to grow': Isro chief V Narayanan defends expanding private sector role
Article Text:
Isro chairman V Narayanan addresses the inaugural session of the 9th Bengaluru Space Expo 2026, in Bengaluru (Picture credit: PTI)

Isro to work with private sector

Target of 50 launches a year

Employee associations seek clarity

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Isro chairman V Narayanan on Monday said the space agency remains a government organisation and dismissed concerns about its privatisation, saying the growing involvement of private companies and startups is part of efforts to expand India’s space ecosystem.His remarks came a day after nine employee associations at Isro centres sought official clarification on the proposed transfer of some manufacturing and operational functions to private entities.Speaking to reporters after the inaugural ceremony of the ninth edition of the Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX), Narayanan said the concerns raised by employees were genuine and that it was the organisation’s responsibility to address them.“So, surely, my colleagues, whatever they have, it is a genuine concern. It is our responsibility to clarify,” he said, as quoted by news agency PTI.Asked about different voices within Isro raising concerns, Narayanan said, “We will address the employees.”Also read: Isro says its 'next chapter' is leading national space ecosystem Narayanan said India’s space programme was about 64-65 years old and that 56 space assets were currently operating in orbit to serve the country.He said the scale of India’s requirements meant that the number of space activities and launches would have to increase substantially.Recalling the space sector reforms introduced six years ago, Narayanan said the government’s approach was to support private companies and startups and expand the overall space ecosystem.“Since the space sector reforms were rolled out six years ago, as per that, we are supposed to hand-hold the private sector, startup companies, and grow the space ecosystem,” he said.He also said Indian industry already had a substantial role in Isro’s launch programmes.“In fact, whenever a PSLV or a GSLV is lifting off, almost 80 per cent budget is invested in Indian industries. A total of 450 industries are working for us,” Narayanan said.At the same time, he stressed that Isro itself had not been privatised.“We are working -- it's a government investment, and we are working there. But the only thing is, we now (have) so many activities. The space ecosystem in the country has to grow and the space economy has to grow,” he said.Narayanan said India’s requirements would eventually require around 50 launch vehicles a year.“The country's requirement is around 50 launch vehicles per year. We have to go ahead,” he said.He recalled that when he joined Isro 43 years ago, the organisation conducted one launch roughly once every three years.“So many activities are going on. Probably one or two things are only known outside, but it is our responsibility to put everything in the Isro side. Fifty launches per year is going to be a reality,” he said.Narayanan added that the target would be achieved “by Indians in India”.The target of 50 launches a year by 2030 has also been cited by IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka, who said the scale would require government and private industry to work together.Also read: Isro will never be privatised, its role won't be diminished - Space Agency & INSPACe chief The nine employee associations had written to Narayanan on September 4 seeking clarification over the direction and basis of the transition towards greater private-sector participation.The associations represent employees at several Isro centres and raised questions over whether launch-vehicle design, development, integration, testing and launch operations would continue as Isro functions or be transferred to private entities.Also read: In a first, 9 Isro staff bodies seek 'written clarity' on private sector shift They also sought clarity on the future role of public-sector units, the transfer or opening of publicly developed technology and infrastructure to private operators, and the respective roles of NSIL and IN-SPACe.The employee bodies expressed concern that a progressive withdrawal of Isro from launch-vehicle and satellite realisation could affect in-house work, recruitment, sanctioned posts and career opportunities.Isro had said on Sunday that suggestions that the agency would be privatised or its importance reduced were “completely baseless and incorrect”.The agency said it would continue as India’s principal institution for advanced space research and technology development, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilities.It also said greater private-sector participation was intended to allow industry to scale mature technologies while Isro focused more on areas including frontier research, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions, and strategic capabilities.
Article Summary: Isro chairman v narayanan said the space agency remains a government organisation. He dismissed concerns about its privatisation, saying the growing involvement of private companies and startups is part of efforts to expand india’s space ecosystem.

Article Title: Silver prices crash over 40% from Rs 4 lakh/kg high to Rs 2.35 lakh, but buyers are still staying away; bigger problem yet to arrive as 2,000 tonnes ordered by Indian dealers risk piling up
Article Text:
Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins.

Silver Demand Weakens

Massive stockpiling of silver

Silver’s Spectacular Fall

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

A huge crash in silver prices should have led to a revival in demand, but investors seem to be staying away. And this has raised a fresh worry ahead of the festive season.Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. The situation comes even as silver prices have dropped by more than 40% from their January peak of over Rs 4 lakh per kg. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the US-Iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.In Mumbai’s spot market, silver was trading at Rs 2.35 lakh per kg earlier this week.Traders and analysts have said that the slowdown in investment demand can be seen across silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs), bars and coins. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses, making them hesitant to make fresh purchases despite the steep correction in prices!Also Read | A couple sold gold for Rs 20 lakh to buy a home, another family got Rs 80 lakh for a US degree and business: How Indians are unlocking value of idle gold sitting in their lockers "Investment demand for silver ETFs, bars and coins has come down. Internationally, prices are unlikely to cross $100 per troy ounce immediately unless the US-Iran war comes to an end. Silver prices are undervalued," Chirag Sheth, global business head, Public Gold Bullion (SG) Pte told ET. "The continuous war between US and Iran has impacted the solar industry, semiconductor industry and EV industry where silver is used. "The weak demand is also creating an inventory problem for domestic players.Indian bullion dealers and refiners have reportedly placed orders for around 2,000 tonnes of silver, which is currently in transit. The additional supplies have raised concerns over a further build-up in stocks. India imports around 7,000 tonnes of silver every year."With no new investors coming in and no immediate signs of prices going up, refiners and bullion dealers are facing a problem internationally as well as in domestic markets," said James Jose, president, Precious Metals Refiners Forum.Silver prices have fallen steadily over the past seven months, following an extraordinary rally that pushed the metal more than 300% higher year-on-year. In January, silver crossed Rs 4 lakh per kg on the Multi Commodity Exchange for the first time."The market is still digesting the aftermath of the speculation-driven frenzy, and this may be prompting investors to stay away after many of them incurred significant losses," said Carsten Menke, head, Next Generation Research, Julius Baer told ET.The outlook for industrial demand is adding to the pressure, with consumption expected to weaken. "A shift to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium and copper, has started, and the growth outlook for Chinese solar module makers, which are the biggest industrial users of silver, is not as strong anymore," Menke said.The ongoing US-Iran war has added to the negative sentiment surrounding silver. If the conflict continues for an extended period, investors may remain cautious. At the same time, expectations of weaker industrial consumption could make a rapid rebound in silver prices difficult.Despite the sharp fall, some long-term investors are once again looking at silver as a way to diversify their portfolios."The market has taken full cognisance of the marked decline in silver prices in recent days. Some investors have shaved off their allocation, while others have prepared for fresh acquisition depending on their views and goals," said Nilanjan Dey, partner, Wishlist Capital.Dey said investors who have a time horizon of five years or longer may look at buying silver ETFs in a staggered manner instead of putting in a large amount at one go. Monthly or fortnightly investments could help spread out the purchase price and reduce the impact of short-term price movements.For first-time investors looking to add precious metals to their portfolios as a diversification from equities, ETFs can provide exposure without the need to hold or manage physical silver. However, Dey warned that investors with a shorter investment horizon should not assume that the recent decline automatically makes silver an attractive buying opportunity.
Article Summary: Silver refiners and bullion dealers are seeing their inventories build up as new investment demand for the metal weakens. Investors who bought the metal when prices were significantly higher are now sitting on substantial losses. Uncertainty over a possible breakthrough in the us-iran war and concerns about subdued industrial demand have added to the pressure.

Article Title: Hailee Steinfeld’s latest career move catches Josh Allen’s attention as Beau Society expands into a new venture
Article Text:
Hailee Steinfeld and Josh Allen (Image via Getty Images)

Hailee Steinfeld expands Beau Society with new merch

Josh Allen shows support for Hailee Steinfeld’s latest move

Hailee Steinfeld has found a new way to turn a personal passion into a growing brand, and Josh Allen is quietly cheering her on. The actress and Buffalo Bills quarterback’s wife has expanded Beau Society beyond her newsletter with a limited merchandise drop. Allen did not need a long public message to show his support. One Instagram Story was enough to get fans talking.Steinfeld’s Beau Society has become more than a newsletter. After reaching its 100th issue on August 28, the actress celebrated the milestone before giving subscribers another reason to pay attention.The latest move is a small clothing collection tied directly to the Beau Society identity. The first drop includes the Beau Society Tee, the “This is BS” hat and the Beau tee.The launch arrived Saturday, with the Beau Society Instagram account sharing photographs of Steinfeld wearing pieces from the collection. Rather than keeping the announcement limited to her own platform, Steinfeld also encouraged readers of her newsletter to check out the limited-edition release.“Surprise! Beau Society merch out now!” read the caption of the post.Steinfeld later described the collection as a limited-edition drop, adding a sense of urgency for followers who want to buy something from the first release."As always, this is a limited-edition drop, so get it while it’s hot," Steinfeld wrote in the 101st issue of her newsletter on Saturday.The move also shows how Beau Society is evolving. What began as a newsletter has developed into a recognizable personal brand, giving Steinfeld a space to connect with followers outside her acting career.Allen’s contribution to the launch was far less flashy, but it still caught attention.The Bills quarterback shared the Beau Society merchandise post on his Instagram Story. There was no lengthy caption or elaborate announcement from Allen. He simply amplified his wife’s new project to his own audience.That low-key gesture fits the way the couple has often shared glimpses of their life while keeping much of it private.Steinfeld recently marked another personal milestone when she reached 100 issues of Beau Society. In that edition, she opened up about the celebration and shared a warm family moment.“I’m writing this issue from a barstool at my kitchen island,” Steinfeld wrote. “Beside me is the most beautiful bouquet my family sent me and my breakfast: a big piece of funfetti cake with pink frosting. I don’t know why, but cake for breakfast seems like the perfect way to ring in Beau Society’s 100th issue!”The couple has also spoken about their life as parents. Allen previously revealed that he and Steinfeld have developed a simple nighttime tradition after their daughter goes to sleep.“We’re trying to limit the screens ‘cause if there’s a screen, she’s over there looking,” Allen said. “When we know that [her] eyes are closed and almost out, my wife and I play the New York Times crossword every night. That’s our little routine that we love doing.”For Steinfeld, Beau Society now appears to be entering another chapter. And with Allen quietly backing her latest venture, the project has plenty of personal meaning behind it.
Article Summary: Hailee steinfeld has expanded beau society beyond her newsletter with a limited merchandise drop. The actress and buffalo bills quarterback's wife has expanded her personal brand into a clothing collection. Allen did not need a long public message to show his support for the move.

Article Title: Samsung India cuts 80-100 jobs as chip prices more than double and smartphone volumes fall 11-12%; another round may come after Diwali, up to 25% of electronics sales and marketing staff at risk
Article Text:
Those affected include director-level officials and team leads at the company's headquarters. (Image for representative purpose only)

Termination letters issued

Rupee depreciation pinches

No layoffs in smartphones team for now

Samsung India Electronics has started laying off its workforce in phases as its core smartphone business faces pressure on sales and margins following a more than twofold increase in memory chip prices. Around 80-100 executives in the television and home appliance businesses have so far been asked to leave, according to reports.Those affected include director-level officials and team leads at the company's headquarters, as well as branch and area managers working across its operating branches, according to the executives.“Up to 25% of its sales and marketing workforce in the electronics business — including offroll employees hired through manpower agencies — could be affected,” one executive told ET on the condition of anonymity.The domestic electronics sales organisation has around 550-600 executives, in addition to the much larger sales workforce handling smartphones. One employee affected by the cuts told the financial daily that termination letters have been issued in small batches on a daily basis over the past few days, with employees being asked to leave without serving their notice periods.As part of the severance package, the company is offering three months' salary, along with an additional month's pay for every year of service.The company's difficulties have also been aggravated by the rupee's nearly 10% decline through FY26, although the currency has remained largely stable during the current fiscal year after reaching a trough in May.The weaker rupee has pushed up the prices of Samsung's smartphones and most of its other electronic products, putting pressure on sales growth. Sales and margin growth across the wider Indian electronics industry are also being affected this year.Industry estimates indicate that smartphone volumes in India have fallen 11-12% year-on-year.Mobile phones contribute around three-fourths of Samsung India's local revenue. At the same time, the South Korean company has struggled to make headway in India's high-value air-conditioner market despite stepping up its efforts this year. This has added to the pressure on its consumer electronics business, which is also dealing with a sharp rise in raw material costs.Samsung is also restructuring its branch network as part of its cost-cutting efforts. Several offices are being merged, with Ranchi and Patna, Delhi and Gurgaon, and Punjab and Chandigarh among the locations being combined. The move has made some positions redundant, according to industry executives.The lack of a semiconductor business in India is being seen as a factor weighing on the performance and manpower outlook of Samsung's local operations. Samsung's semiconductor business has also made it one of only three Asian stocks with a trillion-dollar market capitalisation.For now, the smartphone division has been spared from the layoffs, the report said. It remains Samsung's biggest business in India, and a recovery in smartphone sales could have a significant impact on the company's overall financial performance in the country.The company's latest super-premium smartphones, the Galaxy Fold and Flip series, have received a positive response, although phones priced at Rs 1 lakh and above account for only 4% of the overall market by volume.Samsung, however, lost ground in the broader domestic smartphone market during April-June, according to the latest data from market tracker Counterpoint Research. The company dropped to third place from second, with Vivo taking the top position and Oppo ranking second in a closely fought market.Counterpoint Research said Samsung has been using aggressive promotions across several key models.Samsung India's total revenue reached Rs 1.1 lakh crore in FY25, a 12% increase from the previous year, according to its latest filings with the Registrar of Companies. Home appliances contributed 11% of sales, making the category the company's second-largest after mobile phones.The company's net profit for FY25 was Rs 11,287 crore, up 38% from the previous fiscal year. Financial results for FY26 are yet to be released.Samsung's global mobile business also faced a setback in the June quarter, turning in an operating loss. Its consumer electronics operations continued to remain under pressure, even as strong demand for memory chips helped drive a sharp rise in semiconductor profits.“There’s manpower rationalisation in the home appliance and television businesses. The second round can happen after Diwali,” said one of the executives cited earlier.“There will be no immediate job cuts in the mobile phone business as this is its bread and butter and the company expects a rebound in sales during Diwali. However, it might get evaluated later.”Samsung raised prices of some smartphone models by 5-10% on Monday. This was the third price increase announced by the company this month.The All India Mobile Retailers’ Association has said repeated price hikes have led to a sharp 40% decline in consumer footfall.Samsung India has also pushed back a proposed merger of its home appliance and television sales teams to the December quarter. Industry executives said the move is expected to help cut costs and reduce management layers. One executive, however, said the proposed merger has been deferred.
Article Summary: Around 80-100 executives in the television and home appliance businesses have so far been asked to leave, according to reports. Those affected include director-level officials and team leads at the company's headquarters. The company's difficulties have also been aggravated by the rupee's nearly 10% decline through fy26.

Article Title: Tom Brady’s $1 billion company adds a major investor as seven time Super Bowl champion expands his business empire
Article Text:

Tom Brady's successful company finds a new investor ahead of the new season as he gears up to return as an analyst

Tom Brady’s diversified investment has only increased ever since he retired from the league

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, has been pretty active with investing his wealth ever since he retired from the league. While his personal life has dominated headlines in the last few years, Tom Brady’s brand NoBull has found a new investor.As per reports, NoBull, a sneaker and athletic apparel company co-owned by entrepreneur Mike Repole and NFL legend Tom Brady, has now been invested by RIA platform services provider Dynasty Financial Partners.Tom Brady’s NoBull has achieved a whopping $1 billion valuation after raising $50 million in funding recently.In a statement, Dynasty Financial Partners CEO Shirl Penney said, “We believe independent advisors are hungry for differentiated private-market opportunities typically only available to the world's largest investors, and as Dynasty continues to more than level the playing field for RIAs that are Powered by Dynasty, we look forward to continuing to selectively bring these unique value-add opportunities to our network of independent RIAs. "In an interview with InvestmentNews, Karim Simplis, director of private markets at Dynasty Financial Partners said, “When you think about Mike [Repole] and his team, their track record [and] billions of exits across a number of different deals for them — NoBull is their next great company that they want to build…”For the unversed, in January 2024, the New England Patriots legend, Tom Brady merged his health and nutrition line TB12 and his apparel brand into NOBULL.The NFL legend became the second-largest shareholder in the company, just behind majority owner Mike Repole, the founder of BodyArmor.In an interview with CNBC, the seven time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady had opened up about partnering with Mike Repole as he said, “I think the piece that really resonates with me is our mindset and how we want to inspire others through action and through challenging them to be the best they can possibly be for themselves…”Tom Brady added, “I thought it was the best opportunity for myself and the brands that I’ve been a part of to make a difference…”As per Forbes, Tom Brady’s net worth is estimated to be between $300 million to $350 million.According to reports, the NFl legend’s investment portfolio spans across professional teams (Las Vegas Raiders, Las Vegas Aces, Birmingham City FC, Birmingham Phoenix, E1 Series Team Brady, Major League Pickleball) and commercial brands (Nobull, TB12, BRADY apparel, CardVault by Tom Brady, Autograph, Aescape, Fanatics, GOLF+, SageSpot).Coupled with his analyst salary, it seems Tom Brady is living a pretty luxurious life with his three children whom he co-parents.

Article Title: US designates 15-year-old Italian tech collective as terror organisation; forcing it to shut down; Company says: Day we discovered, ⁠we are ...
Article Text:
US designates 15-year-old Italian tech collective as terror organisation (AI-generated image for representation purpose)

A collective built on privacy-focused digital tools

​

Washington's designation set off a chain of consequences

A group that says it tried to keep operating

Weighing the risk to users over continued operation

For 15 years, Autistici/Inventati had operated as a volunteer-run refuge for activists and campaigners seeking alternatives to commercial online platforms. Then a US terrorism designation forced the Italian technology collective to shut its doors. According to a recent report by the news agency Reuters, the group has now announced that it will end its services after the designation triggered the suspension of its .org domain and the closure of its bank account. The shutdown affects a substantial user base. The closure impacts about 16,000 mailboxes, 1,500 websites, 5,500 mailing lists and 10,000 blogs, according to figures from the US State Department.Founded in 2001, Autistici/Inventati, known as A/I, provided privacy-focused email, websites, mailing lists and blogging services. Its stated purpose was to offer activists, campaigners and others a space outside mainstream commercial platforms, where data practices and content policies are often shaped by corporate interests.The organisation described itself in different terms than US officials. A/I rejected the terrorism designation, describing itself as a collective of volunteers and digital activists that provides digital self-defence tools for activists, individuals, groups and associations.The US designated the group on August 26, alleging it provided support to extremist activists and organisations through services including email accounts, websites and communications tools. The allegation triggered a rapid sequence of institutional responses that A/I said left it unable to continue operating, the Reuters report noted.Two days after the designation, autistici.org became unreachable after Public Interest Registry (PIR), the US-based operator of the .org domain, placed it on serverHold status. PIR said it was legally required to suspend the domain following the designation, framing its action as compliance rather than an independent judgment on the group's activities.The financial consequences followed soon after. Banca Etica, an Italian lender where the collective held an account, subsequently suspended the account, citing sanctions-related risks. The bank criticised what it described as the use of US sanctions for political purposes, a characterisation that placed it at odds with the rationale behind Washington's designation.In a statement announcing the closure, A/I told Reuters it had hoped to continue operating but could no longer do so responsibly. The collective described its initial response to the designation as one of defiance rather than immediate retreat. "The day we discovered we had been designated a global terrorist organisation, we promised that we would try to resist as long as this was possible," the collective said.That resistance, however, gave way to concerns about the people connected to the organisation rather than the organisation itself. A/I said it had "a responsibility to protect our users" and could not ignore the risk that people associated with the organisation might face legal or financial consequences.The collective's explanation centred on the potential fallout for people only loosely connected to its work, rather than on the designation's direct effect on its own infrastructure. "The possibility that our work may cause legal and financial consequences to those who are close to us, or even only have something to do with us, leaves us no choice," it said.The statement did not detail what legal avenues, if any, remain open to challenge the designation.
Article Summary: Us designates 15-year-old italian tech collective as terror organisation. The designation triggered the suspension of its.org domain and the closure of its bank account. The closure impacts about 16,000 mailboxes, 1,500 websites, 5,500 mailing lists and 10,000 blogs.

Article Title: iPhone 18 launch event on September 9: How, when and where to watch Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ 2026 event
Article Text:
When and where to watch Apple’s ‘Surprise and Shine’ event

How to watch Apple iPhone 18 launch event

What to expect from iPhone 18 series launch event

Apple will host its iPhone 18 launch event, titled “Surprise and Shine”, on September 9, 2026 and this year’s keynote carries extra weight as it is the first major public moment for the company’s new CEO John Ternus. Also, this year’s event is also said to witness the launch of the first foldable iPhone. The company will be launching the all new iPhone 18 series which is said to comprise iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. Along with this, Apple is also expected to debut its first-ever foldable smartphone likely to be called iPhone Ultra Alongside the iPhones, Apple is likely to announce the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, a ceramic edition, and new health features. The AirPods 5 may debut with heart-rate tracking, while a new Apple Home Hub could expand Apple’s smart-home ecosystem.The event kicks off at 10am PT (10.30 pm IST) and will be held at Apple Park in Cupertino, California. Viewers can stream the keynote live through YouTube, the Apple Events page, and the Apple TV app, among other methods.Those interested can tune in and watch the iPhone 17 launch live from multiple platforms:* Apple's official website (Apple.com)* The Apple TV app* Apple's official YouTube channelThe spotlight will be on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, expected to feature a mechanical variable aperture camera, the TSMC 2nm A20 Pro chip, improved battery life, and a new Sky Blue titanium finish. Apple is also set to unveil its first foldable iPhone Ultra, with a 7.8-inch book-style display, side Touch ID, and premium pricing around $2,500.Apple’s first foldable smartphone: The device drawing the most attention is Apple's first foldable, which most reports expect to be called iPhone Ultra. Leaks point to a 7.8-inch inner display that opens like a book and a roughly 5.3-inch cover screen, with the A20 Pro chip and 12GB of memory. Rumours suggest two 48MP rear cameras and no telephoto lens, which would be an odd omission at this price. There are also claims that authentication falls back to Touch ID rather than Face ID.Apple iPhone 18 series: The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are widely tipped as a spec-bump year. Reports point to a 2nm A20 Pro with packaging changes meant to help thermals, Apple's own C2 modem, a slightly larger camera bump and a dark cherry finish. A variable-aperture rear camera is rumoured to be a Pro Max exclusive, and under-display Face ID has been floated without much backing. Pricing is the bigger question. With memory costs climbing, Samsung and Google have each raised phone prices by about $100, and Gurman expects Apple to follow, which would put the iPhone 18 Pro near $1,199. Other estimates run steeper.Apple Watches and AirPods: Apple Watch Series 12 is expected to be a light update, with talk of a health sensor tied to a fluoroelastomer band, while the Apple Watch Ultra 4 may get a redesign. AirPods 5 look likely, in ANC and non-ANC versions. The camera-equipped AirPods that leaked in a macOS Tahoe release candidate are still reported as a 2027 product.The home devices are the bigger unknown. Reports mention a refreshed Apple TV 4K, a new HomePod mini and a home hub with a seven-inch screen. Gurman reports Apple is reworking the accessory sections in its retail stores, which he takes as a sign of more than routine updates. An OLED iPad mini remains a wildcard.
Article Summary: When and where to watch apple’s ‘surprise and shine’ event on september 9, 2026. Viewers can stream the keynote live through youtube, the apple events page, and the apple tv app. The event kicks off at 10am pt (10.30 pm ist) and will be held at apple park in cupertino, california.

Article Title: As Samsung turns 30 in India, JB Park lauds country's role as Global Innovation Hub for the company
Article Text:
JB Park, Samsung South West Asia President and CEO

India has evolved from being a market where global technologies were introduced to a country helping imagine, engineer and develop technology for the world, Samsung South West Asia President and CEO JB Park said as Samsung marks 30 years in India. “What inspires me most about India is that it constantly exceeds expectations,” Park said. “Today, we don’t look at India just as a market of 1.4 billion people. We see India as a place where the future of technology is being imagined, developed and led.”Samsung entered India in 1995. Over the past three decades, as India transformed into one of the world’s fastest-growing digital and innovation economies, Samsung expanded its manufacturing footprint, strengthened its research and design capabilities and invested in building an innovation ecosystem in the country.“The story of Samsung in India has never been about selling products. It has been about growing together,” Park said. “But more importantly, we evolved from bringing technology to India to creating technology with India.”“India challenges us to innovate differently,” Park said. “Building products for a country of this scale and diversity means designing solutions that are intuitive, inclusive and relevant to millions of people with very different needs.Those innovations often go on to benefit consumers around the world.”As artificial intelligence transforms consumer technology, Samsung’s engineers in India are also collaborating with global teams to develop next-generation AI experiences.“AI will only be meaningful if it solves real problems for real people. And, there are few places that challenge us to do that better than India,” Park said. Samsung’s investments in India have also extended beyond manufacturing and R&D to talent, skills, education and innovation.“Technology does not create progress on its own. People do,” Park said. “We believe human potential is the most important technology platform of all.”As Samsung marks three decades in the country, he said the company's legacy in India should ultimately be measured not only by the products, manufacturing ecosystem and research capabilities it has helped build, but by the people and ideas it has helped nurture.“I don’t believe our legacy will ultimately be defined by the devices we made,” Park said. “I believe it will be defined by the dreams we helped unlock.” “If Samsung can play even a small role in helping shape that generation, it would be our greatest achievement in India,” he added. “Because the most enduring technologies are not always the ones we build. Sometimes, they are the ideas we ignite in people.”
Article Summary: Samsung entered india in 1995. Over the past three decades, as india transformed into one of the world’s fastest-growing digital and innovation economies. Samsung expanded its manufacturing footprint, strengthened its research and design capabilities and invested in building an innovation ecosystem in the country.

Article Title: In 2006, Google's senior VP emailed Steve Jobs seeking permission to hire a former Apple executive; Jobs replied: We would have a problem if...
Article Text:
In 2006, Google's senior VP emailed Steve Jobs seeking permission to hire a former Apple executive​

Steve Jobs wanted to know exactly what Jean-Marie Hullot would build in Paris

On 28 March 2006, Alan Eustace, then Google 's senior vice president of engineering, wrote an email that reads less like a hiring note and more like a request for royal assent. Google wanted to offer Jean-Marie Hullot, the French engineer who had been CTO of Apple 's applications division until the previous year, a job running a small engineering centre in Paris. Before anything moved, Eustace asked Steve Jobs for his blessing. Bill Campbell, Sergey Brin and Larry Page were on copy.The exchange, surfaced by Internal Tech Emails, goes well past politeness. Eustace noted that Hullot had agreed to abide by his non-solicit and non-compete terms, that he loved Apple, and would not do anything to hurt Jobs or the company. Then the part that has aged badly. Google's relationship with Apple mattered so much, Eustace wrote, that if the hire threatened it in any way, Google would pass on the opportunity. A rival CEO was being handed a quiet veto over Google's hiring.Jobs took eleven days to answer, and when he did, on 9 April, he asked a single question. What would Jean-Marie be working on? "We would have a problem if it is related to cell phone handsets, etc," he wrote.The timing explains the nerves. The iPhone was still nine months from being unveiled, and Hullot was among the people who had pushed hardest for Apple to build a phone in the first place.Satisfied with the answer, Jobs wrote back the next day that the arrangement would be fine with him.It did not hold. On 25 April, Eustace returned to say Hullot wanted to bring four engineers who had worked for him at Apple's Paris office, and offered to cancel the entire thing if Jobs objected. Jobs' reply the following day ran to nine words: Google should strongly prefer not to hire these guys. On 23 May, Eustace confirmed that Google would not open a Paris engineering centre at all. Hullot never joined. He built the photo startup Fotonauts, later Fotopedia, and died in 2019.These no-poach emails became evidence in a $415 million wage suppression caseThe thread entered the public record as a plaintiff's exhibit in In re: High-Tech Employee Antitrust Litigation, the 2011 class action in which roughly 64,000 engineers accused Apple, Google, Intel and Adobe of agreeing not to poach each other's staff to hold salaries down. Judge Lucy Koh rejected an initial $324.5 million settlement as too low and approved $415 million in September 2015, about $5,770 per worker.Tim Sweeney, reading it this week, needed two words: blatantly illegal.
Article Summary: In 2006, google's senior vp emailed steve jobs seeking permission to hire a former apple executive. Jobs wanted to know exactly what jean-marie hullot would build in paris. On 23 may, eustace confirmed that google would not open a paris engineering centre at all.

What once seemed distant is becoming possible. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may soon help humans communicate with animals. But the technology is also raising an ethical question over whether animals have a right to privacy. Machine learning models are helping researchers catalogue and reproduce animal sounds, allowing scientists to identify patterns in how animals communicate. But researchers writing in Springer Nature warn that collecting and decoding these signals could itself raise ethical concerns.the researchers wrote.Machine learning is helping researchers sort large collections of animal sounds and identify patterns that can be difficult to detect manually. Biologist Vittorio Baglione, who has spent years studying carrion crow calls, said he was struck by how AI models could sort his recordings and identify common features in different calls.One call, which Baglione described as essentiallyis used by crows to summon others to defend a nest, he told Bloomberg.The ability to understand such signals could eventually make communication with animals possible. But researchers warn that the same technology could also be misused.One concern involvesthe practice of broadcasting recorded animal calls into the wild. A person could use an imitation of a familiar call to influence an animal’s behaviour without fully understanding what the signal means.Baglione warned that hunters or others with malicious intentions could misuse the technology.he said.César Rodríguez-Garavito, director of the More-Than-Human Life, or MOTH, Program at New York University, has also raised concerns about playback technology.In a 2025 report on AI systems for animal communication, Rodríguez-Garavito said the technology could expose animals to large numbers of people seeking to communicate with them or potentially allow the animals to be weaponised.Previous playback experiments have shown how distressing an artificial call can be. In 2007, zoologist Katy Payne acknowledged that she had caused an elephant significant distress after playing a recording of its dead grandfather’s voice.The example highlights the difficulty of using animal communication technology responsibly. A system may reproduce a call accurately without researchers fully understanding its meaning or the effect it could have on the animal.Despite those concerns, researchers and technology developers continue to pursue systems that could establish communication between humans and animals.There is currently a $10 million reward for a project that can establish communication with an animal without the animal recognising that it is communicating with humans.Private equity billionaire Jeremy Coller, who funds the Coller Doolittle Challenge, said at the challenge’s latest prize event in June that humans could reach the goal within the next decade.he said.If that happens, the technology could change how humans understand animal communication. It could also force researchers to consider whether understanding an animal’s signals gives humans the right to use information the animals may never have intended to share.

Article Text:
Apple foldable iPhone (Representiave image)

What more Apple is expected to launch at September 9 event

Apple will hold its "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, September 9, at 10.30 pm IST at Apple Park in Cupertino, and this year the lineup breaks a pattern the company has followed for close to a decade. Three phones are expected on stage: the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and Apple's first foldable, which leaks have settled on calling the iPhone Ultra. The standard iPhone 18, the iPhone 18e and the second-generation iPhone Air have reportedly been pushed to spring 2027. That leaves the entire autumn lineup sitting at the expensive end of the range, with no cheaper model arriving a week later to take the pressure off.The event is also the first that John Ternus will host as chief executive, after taking over from Tim Cook on September 1, and he inherits an awkward pricing situation. Memory costs have climbed steeply through 2026, Apple has already raised prices on Macs and iPads in June, and the iPhone has so far been shielded from that. Most estimates now point to increases of Rs 9,000 to Rs 26,000 over last year's equivalents in dollar terms, with the foldable landing in a bracket no iPhone has occupied before.Preorders are expected on Saturday, September 12, rather than the usual Friday, which falls on September 11 this year, with retail sales starting Friday, September 18. India is expected to be part of the first wave for the Pro models, though foldable availability at launch is less certain.The iPhone Ultra is a book-style foldable that opens wider than it is tall, closer to an iPad mini cut in half than to the tall Android foldables sold here. Reports point to a 5.4 to 5.5-inch outer screen and a 7.8-inch inner display, a titanium frame, and a body around 4.5mm thick when open and roughly 9mm when shut. That is thinner than the iPad Pro and close to the thickness of a current Pro Max, which is the specific claim worth testing in person.Two things had to go to get there. There is no room for the Face ID module, so authentication moves to a Touch ID power button of the sort the iPad Air and iPad mini already use. There is also no telephoto lens, leaving a 48-megapixel main and a 48-megapixel ultra-wide on the back, positioned so they work whether the phone is open or shut. Both screens get their own front camera.Most of Apple's engineering effort has reportedly gone into the crease. A liquid metal hinge, ultra-thin glass, a structural glass mid-frame and an optically clear adhesive that fills micro-cracks over time are all in play, with a target crease depth below 0.15mm. The intent is not just an invisible crease out of the box but one that stays invisible after a year of folding, which is where every rival has struggled. A magnetic Apple Pencil was prototyped and reportedly dropped over concerns the tip would mark the inner display.Software is the other open question. iOS 27 is expected to bring side-by-side apps, iPad-style landscape layouts and sidebars, and beta code already references hinge angle detection, which suggests something similar to Samsung's Flex Mode. Apple has been pushing developers towards app adaptability for months. Whether third-party apps actually stretch properly on day one will decide how this phone reviews.The iPhone 18 Pro keeps the 6.3-inch size and the camera plateau introduced last year, so this is an internal upgrade rather than a redesign. Cases from the 17 Pro are expected to fit. The A20 Pro moves to a 2nm process and is tipped to be about 18 per cent faster and 30 per cent more efficient than the A19 Pro, with a wider memory interface and a larger cache for the efficiency cores.The camera change is the one that matters. The main sensor is expected to get a variable aperture, letting the phone stop down in harsh light and open up indoors, which is the first meaningful shift in iPhone exposure control in years. A three-layer stacked sensor is also rumoured, which would help with readout speed and low light. The Camera Control button is reportedly being simplified, with the capacitive layer removed after two years of complaints about accidental launches.The Dynamic Island is expected to shrink by around 35 per cent, from roughly 20.7mm to 13.5mm, though at least one leaker maintains that change has slipped to next year. Under-display Face ID, rumoured for a while, is not happening. Dark Cherry is the headline colour, alongside a light blue and silver, and leaked SIM trays suggest black may be missing from the lineup entirely.The Pro Max is where the battery gains land. A 5,567mAh cell would be nearly 10 per cent larger than last year's 5,088mAh unit, and paired with the 2nm chip and the more efficient LTPO+ panel, it should stretch what is already the longest-lasting iPhone. Units sold in China are expected to carry a smaller 5,391mAh cell because a physical SIM slot takes up room.That capacity comes with weight. The phone is expected to be about 0.25mm thicker and seven grams heavier at roughly 240 grams, with a camera plateau that grows from 11.23mm to 11.54mm. Some reports suggest the variable aperture camera may be exclusive to this model, which would be unusual but not without precedent, since the 15 Pro Max was the only phone in its year to get the tetraprism telephoto.Beyond the phones, Apple is expected to show the Apple Watch Series 12 with a ceramic case option returning, the Apple Watch Ultra 4, and the AirPods 5 with a new H3 chip. A smart home hub, a refreshed Apple TV and a new HomePod mini are all in the running as well, though those may be held for a smaller event later in the year. Software dates should be announced at the same time. iOS 27, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27 and the rest are expected to reach existing devices in the week following the event, with September 14 the most cited date.
Article Summary: Apple expected to unveil iphone 18 pro, 18 pro max and first foldable at september 9 event. Leaks have settled on the iphone ultra, which is expected to have a 7.8-inch oled display. Apple will also unveil new ipads and mac computers at the event. India is expected to be part of the first wave for the pro models, though foldable availability at launch is less certain.

Article Title: SAP has a message for all software companies, after stock goes down by over 20%: Pendulum will swing back, as ...
Article Text:
SAP has a message for all software companies

SAP stock rebounds after SaaS sell-off

SAP says AI will not easily replace mission-critical software

SAP sees another challenge emerging: the rising cost of using AI

SAP is changing how it charges for AI

SAP is telling the software industry not to write off traditional SaaS companies as AI changes how businesses build and buy software. Despite SAP's stock falling by more than 20% over the past year amid the wider “SaaSpocalypse”, SAP global president of customer success and Americas Jan Gilg believes the sell-off has gone too far. “As usual, I feel the pendulum will swing back,” Gilg told Business Insider. Gilg further added that there will be “users,” “losers and winners” and said he believes SAP will be among the winners.The comments come as AI tools from companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI raise questions about whether businesses will continue paying for traditional software. SAP, Salesforce and Workday have all faced pressure as investors assess how AI could change the software market.SAP's shares have recovered strongly after the company reported its latest earnings in late July. The stock has risen roughly 40% since the results, helped by cloud growth and progress in business AI.Gilg described the earlier sell-off as “a bit of an overreaction on the entire industry.” He said SAP is responding by investing in AI and data while also changing how it charges customers.“Everybody has AI on the agenda right now,” Gilg said.One concern during the SaaSpocalypse has been the rise of “vibe coding”, where AI tools can help people create software without traditional programming methods. Gilg said SAP does not currently see customers replacing its software this way, particularly when it comes to critical business systems.“It's really multifaceted. On the one side, there was the idea that customers will vibe code their software themselves rather than buying packaged software. We don't see that frankly,” Gilg said. “We don't see that, especially for mission-critical purposes. It's not just about features and functions. It's about auditability, governance, and the maintenance of the software.”He said SAP's role could become more important as companies look for ways to connect AI with business data and existing systems.Gilg said companies are already seeing higher “token costs”, referring to the amount of AI usage they pay for. He expects businesses to look more closely at whether their AI spending produces measurable results.“Customers are seeing token costs go through the roof already,” Gilg said. “How do you measure and control that, and how do you show an outcome for that? Budgets won't necessarily increase. It will still have to come from somewhere. Therefore, the scrutiny will become much, much bigger.”“We do see new players out there from Anthropic, OpenAI, Palantir, and so on,” Gilg said. “That's going to be the battlefield of the future.”SAP is also changing parts of its pricing strategy as AI becomes a bigger part of its products. The company is moving some services from traditional subscription models toward consumption-based pricing, where customers pay according to how much they use.“What outcome are they driving?” Gilg said. “That's how we charge the consumption of those agents, which is very transparent to customers. Also, it's much easier to justify why they would actually pay for it. That's the current model many are following.”
Article Summary: Sap's jan gilg says the sell-off of saas companies has gone too far. He believes there will be “users,” “losers and winners” in the software market. Sap is responding by investing in ai and data while changing how it charges customers.

Article Title: Duolingo launches ‘learn English from Punjabi’ course
Article Text:
Duolingo partners with Airtel to offer 12-month super subscription

Duolingo, the world’s leading mobile learning platform, has announced the launch of its new “Learn English from Punjabi” literacy course, aimed at making English learning more accessible to Punjabi speakers in India and across the globe. The course went live on September 7, 2026, and is now available on the Duolingo app.Spoken by more than 100 million people worldwide, Punjabi is one of the most widely spoken languages, with vibrant communities in India, Canada, the UK, the US, and Australia. Written in Gurumukhi script, Punjabi carries a rich literary and cultural heritage. The new course allows learners to begin their English journey directly from Gurumukhi, helping them build skills for education, careers, and global connections.This marks Duolingo’s second regional language course for North India after Hindi, and adds to its growing portfolio of regional offerings, which already includes Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, and Tamil.Karandeep Singh Kapany, Regional Marketing Director for India and South East Asia, said: “Being able to launch this course in my mother tongue is incredibly meaningful and a moment of real pride for me. Punjabis have long embraced opportunities beyond borders.By making English learning available in Punjabi, we’re helping remove language barriers and enabling more people to access the opportunities that English can unlock. ”In another news, recently Duolingo partnered with Airtel to provide 12 months of Super Duolingo at no additional cost to Airtel’s 376 million subscribers.The partnership will give Airtel customers access to Duolingo’s premium ad-free learning experience, including unlimited energy, AI-powered real-time speaking practice, personalised exercises, and mistakes review. The subscription will be available across mobile, Wi-Fi, and DTH services, accessible through the Airtel Thanks App, with no credit card required.Language skills are increasingly becoming gateways to education, careers, and global opportunities. Airtel’s collaboration with Duolingo extends its focus on differentiated customer experiences by offering millions of users an engaging way to build language skills and develop consistent learning habits.
Article Summary: Duolingo partners with airtel to offer 12-month super subscription to super duolingo. Punjabi is one of the most widely spoken languages, with vibrant communities in india, canada, the uk, the us, and australia. The new course allows learners to begin their english journey from gurumukhi.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works



Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies

AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
